name: JD Vance
role: Yale Law graduate, Hillbilly Elegy author, Ohio senator (2023–2025), and 50th vice president (2025–). The board is his public stances, not every vote.

links.label: Political positions of JD Vance
Washington Post profile of Vance’s radicalization

portrait.author: Daniel Torok / Official White House Photo

name: Tariffs & industrial policy
role: Economic nationalist: tariffs, reshoring, and a weaker-dollar openness so factories can compete. As vice president he defended Trump’s tariff program as self-reliance.

links.label: NPR analysis of Vance’s economic policy
New York Times on the dollar

name: Labor unions
role: Backed the 2023 UAW strike and talks up worker councils, while opposing the PRO Act. The AFL-CIO scored his Senate record at 0%.

links.label: Politico on Vance’s labor-populist project
AFL-CIO legislative scorecard

name: Big Tech antitrust
role: Wants Google broken up, implies Meta should be split, and praised Biden FTC chair Lina Khan. Co-introduced a bill to tax giant mergers.

links.label: The Hill on praise for Lina Khan
Stop Subsidizing Giant Mergers Act

name: Keeping the ACA
role: Says he does not intend to repeal the Affordable Care Act, backed an insulin cap and Medicare drug negotiation, and falsely claimed Trump “salvaged Obamacare.”

links.label: Politico on Vance’s health-care record
NBC News fact-check of “salvaged Obamacare”

name: Social Security cuts
role: Reporting says he once backed benefit cuts, then ditched that in the Senate race. By 2024 he opposed cuts and privatization and leaned on birth rates for solvency.

links.label: HuffPost on abandoning support for cuts
Newsweek on his 2024 Social Security position

name: Climate action
role: In 2020 he treated climate as a real problem and doubted natural gas as the answer. By 2022 he rejected a “crisis,” pushed fossil expansion, and sought to kill EV credits.

links.label: Politico on the climate shift and oil money
The Hill on eliminating EV tax credits

name: Higher minimum wage
role: Broke with supply-side orthodoxy to support raising the federal minimum wage as part of an economic-nationalist worker pitch.

links.label: Washington Post on Vance and Republican business elites

name: National abortion ban
role: In 2022 he wanted abortion illegal nationally. In 2024 he backed mifepristone access, said states should decide, promised a Trump veto — then claimed he had “never” supported a national ban.

links.label: NBC News chronology of six abortion statements
CNN on the 2022 national-illegality statement
NBC News on the national-ban veto

name: Family & natalism
role: Wants the state to push marriage and births: a $5,000 child credit, hostility to universal daycare, and a long critique of childless elites he later called sarcastic but true.

links.label: CNN review of childlessness remarks
CBS News on the $5,000 child tax credit

name: Extra votes for parents
role: In 2021 he floated giving children votes that parents would cast. He later called it a thought experiment and backed away during the 2024 campaign.

links.label: ABC News on tax treatment of childless adults

name: Gun rights
role: Favors abolishing ATF, repealing the National Firearms Act, a national stand-your-ground law, and more school security. After a Georgia shooting he called shootings a “fact of life.”

links.label: Ohio Gun Owners candidate survey
CNN on “fact of life” and school security

name: Red-flag laws
role: In 2018 he said clearly unstable people should not have guns. In 2022 he opposed red-flag laws and letting judges or psychiatrists disarm someone as “mentally defective.”

links.label: ABC News comparison of Vance and Walz on guns

name: LGBTQ rights
role: Opposes the Respect for Marriage Act, proposed a federal felony for specified gender-transition surgery on minors, and rejects an “X” passport marker and census gender-identity questions.

links.label: NBC News overview of LGBTQ record
Cleveland.com on the minor-transition-care bill

name: Vaccine & mask mandates
role: Called Ohio State’s COVID vaccine rule an invasion of medical privacy and introduced a bill to bar federal mask mandates on airlines, transit, and schools.

links.label: Columbus Dispatch op-ed on Ohio State’s vaccine mandate
WLWT on the federal anti-mask-mandate bill

name: Immigration restriction
role: In 2012 he attacked GOP deportation talk as hostile to nonwhite voters. By 2021 he wanted a wall, no amnesty, and mass removal, including of TPS holders he called “illegal.”

links.label: CNN on the deleted 2012 immigration post
New York Times on “create stories”

name: Official English
role: In 2023 he introduced a bill to make English the official language of the United States. Introduction is not enactment.

links.label: NPR guide to Vance’s major positions

name: China as principal threat
role: Calls China the largest U.S. threat and wants resources, weapons, and attention pivoted to East Asia rather than open-ended European wars.

links.label: Voice of America on “biggest threat”
Nikkei Asia on prioritizing Taiwan over Ukraine

name: Ukraine military aid
role: Does not “really care” what happens to Ukraine next to fentanyl at home, voted against a 2024 aid package, and wants a freeze, neutrality, and territorial concessions.

links.label: Vance’s New York Times essay opposing further aid
NBC News on territorial concessions

name: Israel alliance
role: Treats Israel as a values ally, wants it armed to finish the Gaza war quickly, and still said U.S. and Israeli interests can diverge — especially on a war with Iran.

links.label: Times of Israel on ending Gaza war and Sunni alignment
Senate office statement on Biden’s Israel policy

name: Iran military action
role: In 2023 he would “absolutely not” authorize force. He later praised hitting Iran “hard,” backed 2025 nuclear-site strikes, and then defended the 2026 Iran war.

links.label: The Hill on opposing authorization of force in 2023
CBS News on defending the 2026 Iran war

name: Iraq War
role: Supported the 2003 invasion as a young Marine, then called that support a mistake and, by 2025, a strategic disaster used to argue for European independence.

links.label: Politico on Republican veterans and anti-interventionism
Deutsche Welle on the “strategic disaster” assessment

name: Afghan refugee admissions
role: During the 2021 withdrawal he objected to prioritizing Afghan admissions and alleged, without evidence, that many ostensible interpreters had helped plant bombs.

links.label: Associated Press on the split over Afghan refugees
Guardian reporting on the 2021 podcast remarks

name: Europe defense burden
role: Would keep the U.S. in NATO if Europeans spend more, called Europe a U.S. “security vassal,” and wants Washington’s focus on China instead.

links.label: The Hill on NATO and Europe
Deutsche Welle on European independence and Iraq

name: Venezuela strikes
role: In 2025–26 he defended U.S. strikes tied to Nicolás Maduro, calling him a wanted fugitive and saying “stolen oil” must be returned.

links.label: Barron’s on Vance, Maduro, and off-ramps

name: AfD engagement
role: Says he is not endorsing Alternative for Germany, then amplifies Elon Musk’s “AfD can save Germany” line and challenges the “Nazi-lite” label.

links.label: Independent on his response to Musk’s AfD essay
Jerusalem Post on Vance’s AfD defense

name: Labour-led Britain
role: Joked that Labour Britain might be the first “truly Islamist” nuclear state. British officials rejected the line even as he stayed cordial with David Lammy.

links.label: Politico Europe on the “Islamist country” remark
BBC on British officials’ response

name: Donald Trump
role: In 2016 he called Trump unfit, “reprehensible,” “cultural heroin,” and privately “America’s Hitler.” By 2021 he had apologized, joined MAGA, and become the running mate.

links.label: Reuters on the anti-Trump-to-running-mate reversal

name: 2020 election result
role: Says Trump won, would have demanded alternate pro-Trump electors rather than certify normally, and at the 2024 debate would not say Trump lost.

links.label: Washington Post on election denial and January 6
NBC News on refusal to acknowledge the 2020 result

name: January 6 clemency
role: Backed broad clemency for January 6 defendants as vice president, then in January 2026 mocked a vigil commemorating the attack.

links.label: Axios on broad January 6 pardons

name: Universities
role: In 2017 he praised universities’ talent and IP. By 2021 they were “the enemy”: a 35% endowment tax, funding cuts, foreign-gift probes, and Orbán-style political control.

links.label: Associated Press on colleges paying Vance and later attacks
CBS News on praise for Orbán’s university decisions

name: Woke institutions
role: Argues business, media, philanthropy, and government form a progressive bloc and wants a “de-woke-ification” he analogizes to denazification.

links.label: Vance’s “Fighting Woke Capital” essay
Senate office release on questioning bank CEOs

name: DOJ & FBI leadership
role: Treats Justice and FBI leadership as a politicized “deep state,” spread a false Trump-wiretap claim, and held Biden DOJ nominees after Trump’s indictment.

links.label: NBC News on holds against DOJ nominees
Business Insider on the FBI wiretap claim

name: Judicial limits on the executive
role: Told a future Trump to fire civil servants and, if courts blocked it, invoke Jackson: the chief justice has made his ruling, now let him enforce it.

links.label: Guardian on the 2025 judicial-power statement
Vox analysis of Vance’s executive ideas

name: Postliberal conservatism
role: Moved from Never Trump conservatism to a postliberal, national-conservative program: family, industry, borders, cultural conflict, and an assertive state.

links.label: Politico on postliberal theorist Patrick Deneen
Politico on seven key intellectual influences
